config.title: Are Berlin’s Attractions Worth It? - FAQ

items.q: Are Berlin's paid tourist attractions worth it?
items.a: **It depends on your group.** LEGOLAND is worth it for young children (about 3 to 10), the Berlin Dungeon suits teenagers who like a scare, and Madame Tussauds works for teens and photo fans. For **adults travelling without children**, the same €20 to €30 buys far more at a real museum, a rooftop view or a walking tour.

items.q: Is Sea Life Berlin still open?
items.a: **No. Sea Life Berlin closed permanently in December 2024**, along with Little BIG City. The AquaDom aquarium that burst in December 2022 was part of the same site and was never rebuilt. The separate **Aquarium Berlin** next to the Zoo is unrelated and still open.

items.q: How much does Madame Tussauds Berlin cost?
items.a: **About €22 online and €29.50 at the door**, for a visit of roughly one to one and a half hours. It is on Unter den Linden 74, two minutes from the Brandenburg Gate. Book online, because it rarely sells out and the door price is clearly higher. (Prices checked 21 August 2026.)

items.q: Is the Berlin Dungeon in English?
items.a: **No, the show is performed largely in German.** It is an 80-minute live-actor experience near Alexanderplatz, from about €18 online, recommended for ages 10 and up. If you do not speak German you will follow the atmosphere and the scares but miss most of the jokes and story.

items.q: Is LEGOLAND Discovery Centre Berlin good for adults or teenagers?
items.a: **No. It is built for children aged about 3 to 10, and adults are admitted only when accompanied by a child.** Teenagers usually find it too young. For families with small kids it is one of the best rainy-afternoon options at Potsdamer Platz, at €19.50 online for two to three hours.

items.q: Where are Berlin's main paid attractions?
items.a: They cluster in the tourist core. **Madame Tussauds** is on Unter den Linden near Brandenburger Tor, the **Berlin Dungeon** is on Spandauer Straße near Alexanderplatz, and **LEGOLAND Discovery Centre** is in the Sony Center at Potsdamer Platz. All three sit a short U-Bahn or S-Bahn ride apart in central Berlin.
